subject: Renewal: cross-region dedicated capacity uplift, EU+APAC onboarding & SLA transition
messages:
From: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@aurorahealth.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + capacity ask — EU & APAC pools for next term

Hi Marissa / Jordan,

As we get close to our annual renewal, AuroraHealth is looking to expand our Dedicated footprint with Redwood. Specifically: add a regional reserved pool in EU (primary) and APAC (secondary) to reduce egress latency for our live inference traffic. Current consumption and asks are attached (aurora-usage-report-q3.csv). High-level asks: 

- EU reserved pool: capacity to sustain 6k tokens/s sustained (p95 peak bursts to 9k) — estimate: 8x A100 equivalent reserved nodes.
- APAC reserved pool: capacity to sustain 2.5k tokens/s sustained (peak bursts to 4k) — estimate: 4x A100 equiv.
- Throughput guarantee: p95 latency target <= 80ms for responses <= 512 tokens in EU; APAC target <= 120ms.
- Failover behavior: automatic cross-region fallback to US-hosted pool when EU/APAC are unavailable; preferring EU->APAC->US order.
- Term ask: extend current committed term by 12 months, include capacity add-on pricing and a 10% committed discount on per-token billing for the reserved pools.

Can you confirm feasibility and a recommended amendment timeline? Procurement wants an outline they can review with finance by next Wednesday. Also including Tom from our cloud partner; he may want to coordinate network peering.

Thanks,
Claire Zhang
Head of Platform
AuroraHealth.ai

Attachments: aurora-usage-report-q3.csv (CSV, 47 KB)
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@aurorahealth.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@cloud-bid.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity ask — EU & APAC pools for next term

Claire — thanks for the detail and the attachment. Internal team reviewed the usage report and we can support the regional expansion. Proposed next steps from Redwood: 

1) Internal kickoff & technical scoping (this week) — Karthik & Jonas to validate node sizing, networking/peering needs, and failover policies.
2) Draft contract amendment & pricing sheet for 12-month extension + committed uplift (I attached an initial draft amendment).
3) Procurement checklist and SOC artifacts — Monica will coordinate SOC2 evidence and retention policy notes.
4) Schedule a 60-minute on-call workshop to align peering and cutover timing (suggest Nov 18 or Nov 22).

High-level answer on feasibility: yes — EU pool (8x reserved A100 equiv) + APAC pool (4x) is workable. We propose a burst window and autoscale policy: reserve for sustained throughput, allow 30% burst capacity from shared burst pool for 10-minute windows. That keeps unit economics predictable while covering transient spikes.

I attached: redwood-term-amendment-draft.pdf (draft pricing & terms) and will loop Karthik for technical specifics below.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-term-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF, 85 KB)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@aurorahealth.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@cloud-bid.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity ask — EU & APAC pools for next term

Team / Claire,

Quick feasibility notes after initial capacity simulation:

- EU pool (8x A100-equivalent) will comfortably sustain 6k tokens/s for the current model mix (50% generate, 50% embed/rerank). We recommend reserving 8 nodes + 2 warm spares for rolling upgrades. Estimated cost delta included in amendment draft.
- APAC pool (4x) looks right for 2.5k sustained, but traffic distribution needs an initial traffic-split rule — suggest 70% EU regional routing, 30% APAC for first 2 weeks of cutover to monitor latencies.
- Latency targets: with our inferred kernel selection & quantized weights we can meet EU p95 <= 75ms for <=512 tokens on the reserved pool. APAC p95 <=110ms is achievable with the proposed sizing and local KV caching.
- Failover: implement health-check-based routing with circuit breaker thresholds (5xx rate >0.5% or p95 >350ms for 3 consecutive 1-min windows triggers region fallback). We will document exact thresholds in the runbook.
- Networking: Tom — we will need BGP peering details or cross-connect timing; recommend starting peering prep 2 weeks before the cutover.

Risks / notes:
- Peak concurrency patterns (long tails from batch imports) can exceed the burst window; recommend Aurora give us a 24-hour high-concurrency sample so we can validate the burst policy.
- If Aurora expects JIT spikes beyond the 30% burst, we should price a larger burst allowance (elastic burst tier) or use reserved burst capacity.

I will prepare the technical runbook draft and SLA appendix (sla-addendum-eu-apac.xlsx).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity ask — EU & APAC pools for next term

Claire / team,

From a CS & compliance perspective — we're aligned. A few operational items for procurement: 

- Data residency: confirm which datasets will be processed in-region vs cross-region. If Aurora requires strict EU-only processing for PII workloads, we'll need to enable Private deployment options for those routes (that will change pricing).
- Audit logs: Aurora requested longer retention in the RFP; we can offer 12 months standard with an add-on for 36 months (see amendment).
- Onboarding timeline: if we start peering prep Nov 22 and validate traffic split during the two-week canary, full cutover by Dec 13 is feasible.
- Acceptance criteria for the rollout: 1) steady-state p95 within SLA for 72 hours; 2) no more than 0.2% 5xx errors across pools; 3) runbook verified by Aurora SREs.

I'll own SOC2 artifact delivery and update the procurement checklist. Marissa — please confirm if we should include Private-route pricing for EU-only PII paths in the amendment or leave that as a separate addendum.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@aurorahealth.ai>, Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@cloud-bid.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: cross-region dedicated capacity uplift, EU+APAC onboarding & SLA transition

Claire / Procurement / Tom — following internal scoping and the runbook draft, here is the consolidated plan and immediate asks: 

Summary of proposed commercial/technical terms:
- Term: 12-month extension (rollforward) to begin on Jan 1 2027.
- EU reserved pool: 8x A100-equivalent reserved nodes + 2 warm spares. Target p95 <= 75ms for <=512 tokens.
- APAC reserved pool: 4x A100-equivalent reserved nodes + 1 spare. Target p95 <= 110ms.
- Autoscale/burst: 30% burst from shared pool for 10-minute windows; optional elastic burst tier priced in amendment.
- Pricing: committed uplift pricing and a 10% committed discount applied to token-based billing for the reserved pools (see redwood-term-amendment-draft.pdf).
- Failover: EU -> APAC -> US routing order; circuit-breaker thresholds and runbook included in sla-addendum-eu-apac.xlsx.
- Onboarding window: Peering prep begins Nov 29; staging traffic split and canary Nov 29–Dec 13; full cutover target Dec 14–20.

Immediate asks from Aurora (to proceed):
1) Procurement to review the attached amendment and confirm acceptance of the committed discount & term. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/example/aurora-redwood-amendment
2) Aurora SRE to share a 24-hour high-concurrency sample (start-of-day PST preferred) so we can validate the burst policy by Nov 25.
3) Tom to provide peering contact and cross-connect timeline by Nov 24.

I'll schedule a combined workshop (SRE + Redwood Ops + Aurora Network) for Nov 30 — calendar invite forthcoming. If procurement needs an alternate timeline we can accelerate pricing approval but cutover dependencies will still require ~2 weeks for peering + validation.

Thanks — ready to move as soon as we have the concurrency sample and signature on the amendment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184
